title: Visitor and Well
premise: Ivo Okonkwo, a rationalist property surveyor, arrives in the drowned-hollow village of Marrow's End to appraise Well House for its last resident, the ancient Miss Verity Ashdown — but the house measures him back, and a bell melted down in 1911 begins ringing each dusk. The village's dead congregation is singing a hymn whose final verse was never written down; anyone who sings along joins them. Ivo, drawn into found family with Verity and her caretaker granddaughter Nell, must transcribe the last verse without voicing it before Verity signs the sale papers that will bind her soul to the well beneath the house. In the end Ivo chooses love over duty: he falsifies the appraisal to void the sale, sings the verse alone as an offering rather than a surrender, and frees the congregation — at the cost of his own unbelief, which dies with the bell.
about_author: Kestrel Zhou is a former land registry clerk from coastal Norfolk who spent six years cataloguing deeds for houses that no longer exist. Their fiction explores what paperwork can't hold.

chapters.title: The Commission
chapters.summary: Third-person limited on Ivo. A London firm assigns him the Ashdown estate appraisal, a job three surveyors have abandoned. He accepts out of professional pride, dismissing rumors of the 'singing parish.' Emotional beat: quiet arrogance established.

chapters.title: Marrow's End
chapters.summary: Ivo drives into a village where every garden grows white flowers he can't identify. The church has no bell tower — just a scar of brick. An old man watches him pass without blinking. Beat: first wrongness, understated dread.

chapters.title: Well House
chapters.summary: Ivo meets Nell Marsh, caretaker and reluctant guide, who warns him not to stay past dark. He notes the well in the kitchen floor, capped with iron, warm to the touch. Beat: attraction and friction between Ivo and Nell.

chapters.title: Miss Ashdown
chapters.summary: Verity Ashdown, ninety-one, lucid and sharp, insists she will sign only when the appraisal is 'honest.' She asks Ivo strange questions: can he carry a tune? Has he ever been mourned? Beat: unease beneath courtesy.

chapters.title: The Inventory
chapters.summary: Ivo surveys room by room; measurements refuse to total correctly, always one foot short. He finds a hymnal with the last page torn out, edges burned. Beat: his methodology begins failing him.

chapters.title: First Ringing
chapters.summary: At dusk a bell tolls though there is no bell. Nell pulls Ivo behind the pantry door; through the crack he sees figures processing across the yard. Beat: terror breaking through skepticism.

chapters.title: The Drowned Parish
chapters.summary: Nell explains over tea: in 1911 the villagers sold their bell to fund the war, but the congregation kept singing anyway, and one by one they stayed. Verity is the only living original voice. Beat: exposition as intimacy; Ivo doesn't believe her, but stays.

chapters.title: Paperwork and Prayer
chapters.summary: Ivo drafts the appraisal; the numbers keep changing overnight. Verity hums three verses of the hymn, stopping precisely where the fourth would begin. Beat: duty pulling him toward completion, curiosity pulling elsewhere.

chapters.title: The Well Breathes
chapters.summary: The iron cap sweats cold. Ivo lowers a plumb line on a whim; it descends far farther than the water table allows and comes up smelling of incense. Beat: the house appraises back.

chapters.title: Nell's Ledger
chapters.summary: Nell shows him generations of records: every surveyor who finished the appraisal signed something. None left the village. Her own mother's name is last. Beat: stakes personal; loyalty vs. truth begins.

chapters.title: Choir Practice
chapters.summary: Ivo attends evensong in the roofless church out of spite. The pews fill with cold. He catches himself mouthing harmony and bites it back. Beat: seduction of belonging.

chapters.title: The Torn Page
chapters.summary: Ivo finds the hymnal's missing page wedged in the well cap's hinge, inked in a child's hand — the final verse, half-legible. He pockets it without telling Nell. Beat: secret-keeping, guilt seeded.

chapters.title: Verity's Bargain
chapters.summary: Verity reveals the sale isn't hers: the diocese wants the land, and her signature completes a covenant begun in 1911. Signing means joining the choir forever. She asks Ivo to make the appraisal honest enough to stop it. Beat: role reversal — the client pleads.

chapters.title: London Calls
chapters.summary: His firm pressures Ivo to close quickly; a rival surveyor is dispatched. Ivo lies about progress for the first time in his career. Beat: duty tightening like a noose.

chapters.title: The Rival Arrives
chapters.summary: Surveyor Dana Whitlock checks into the inn, all efficiency. At dusk she hears the bell and walks toward it smiling. Ivo drags her back; she remembers nothing. Beat: external threat, protective instinct.

chapters.title: Verse One Through Three
chapters.summary: Ivo transcribes the known verses from Verity's memory, learning their structure — each verse a name, each name a soul held. The last verse holds the whole congregation. Beat: horror as liturgy; intellectual dread.

chapters.title: What the Well Wants
chapters.summary: Dreams pull Ivo toward the kitchen at night. The well shows him reflections of people standing behind him. Nell finds him sleepwalking, hand on the cap. Beat: intimacy deepens as she saves him.

chapters.title: Found Family
chapters.summary: A quiet chapter: cooking, repairs, Verity teaching Nell and Ivo a card game from 1908. For one evening the horror recedes. Beat: warmth that makes the coming losses land.

chapters.title: Dana Signs
chapters.summary: Whitlock, compromised, files a preliminary valuation favorable to the diocese. Legal machinery begins turning; a signing date is set in ten days. Beat: clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: The Second Ringing
chapters.summary: The bell rings at noon now, not dusk. The processions come closer to the house. White flowers bloom through the kitchen floorboards around the well. Beat: escalation, sanctuary shrinking.

chapters.title: Half a Verse
chapters.summary: Ivo deciphers more of the torn page: the last verse is a question the singers must answer, and answering aloud is the trap. He tests a line silently and the well goes utterly still, listening. Beat: discovery and peril braided.

chapters.title: Verity Falters
chapters.summary: Verity begins humming the fourth verse in her sleep. Nell begs Ivo to use whatever he found. He denies having the page; the lie costs him Nell's trust. Beat: loyalty vs. truth turns inward.

chapters.title: The Diocese Man
chapters.summary: A solicitor arrives to witness the signing, immune somehow — deaf to the bell. Ivo realizes disbelief is armor, and his own is cracking. Beat: thematic thesis stated in plot.

chapters.title: Confession
chapters.summary: Ivo admits the page to Nell. She is furious, then relieved; together they read it by lamplight. Two lines are missing, eaten by rust. Beat: reconciliation, renewed partnership.

chapters.title: Into the Records
chapters.summary: They search the village archive for the composer: a schoolmistress, Ruth Adeyemi, who wrote the verse for her drowned students. Her grave is under the well. Beat: history becomes geography.

chapters.title: Ruth's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: In a buried schoolroom off the well shaft (Ivo descends on a rope), they find slate boards with the full verse. As he copies it, the choir below begins to harmonize with his pencil scratches. Beat: climax approach; awe and terror.

chapters.title: The Rope
chapters.summary: Something below tugs the rope. Nell hauls Ivo up as hands — patient, not violent — try to keep him. He keeps the slate rubbing clenched in his teeth. Beat: physical set-piece, breathless.

chapters.title: Dana Again
chapters.summary: Whitlock, now hollow-eyed, steals the transcription to trade for her own release. The diocese man burns it in front of her. She runs into the procession at dusk. Beat: cost of betrayal; grief.

chapters.title: Signing Day Eve
chapters.summary: Verity dresses in her best, at peace. She gives Ivo her mother's ring and asks him to remember her singing, not her silence. Beat: elegiac calm before storm.

chapters.title: The Signature
chapters.summary: The solicitor arrives; papers spread on the kitchen table above the well. Verity signs — then Ivo produces his amended appraisal declaring the property unsound, voiding the covenant legally. The bell screams. Beat: climax pivot, love against duty enacted.

chapters.title: What the Bell Demands
chapters.summary: The void bargain needs a voice offered freely. The house floods with congregants; Nell begins to sing along, entranced. Ivo clamps a hand over her mouth as the last verse rises in him. Beat: highest tension.

chapters.title: The Last Verse
chapters.summary: Ivo sings the final verse alone — not the trap-answer, but Ruth's true ending, a benediction he reconstructed from the slates. He offers it for the dead, not with them. The well drinks the sound. Beat: sacrifice and transcendence.

chapters.title: Silence
chapters.summary: The bell stops mid-toll. The congregation bows and dissolves like breath off glass. Verity's chair is empty except for the ring, returned. Nell weeps; Ivo cannot stop shaking. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: The diocese man leaves confused, paperwork inexplicably rejected. Whitlock is found at the bus stop with no memory and a hymn she'll never place. The flowers begin to die. Beat: decompression.

chapters.title: The Appraisal
chapters.summary: Ivo files his honest report: the house is worthless, the well bottomless, the village uninhabitable by any market logic. His firm fires him. He laughs all the way out of the building. Beat: freedom through ruin.

chapters.title: Staying On
chapters.summary: Ivo doesn't leave. He and Nell repair the roofless church into an open-air memorial, naming every singer from the ledgers. Verity's grave joins Ruth's beside the capped well. Beat: found family formalized.

chapters.title: One Foot Short
chapters.summary: Ivo re-measures the house; now every room totals exactly right. The hymnal's torn page regrows blank. Some things only exist while they're needed. Beat: quiet wonder, theme resolved.

chapters.title: The New Bell
chapters.summary: The village casts a small new bell, inscribed with Ruth Adeyemi's name. At its first ringing, it sounds ordinary — just bronze and rope. Everyone cries anyway. Beat: healing without erasure.

chapters.title: What Ivo Believes Now
chapters.summary: Final reflective chapter in Ivo's voice via letter to his old firm. He still won't say he believes — but he listens now, and when the wind moves through the open church, he never hums along. Beat: transformed skeptic, thematic closure.
